step.env: Shell profile — the variable the config reads

notes.claudeCode: Use single quotes so the ${'{'}KNOWLEDGE_API_KEY{'}'} placeholder is stored, not the key itself. Check with `claude mcp list`, then `/mcp` inside a session.
notes.codex: Codex reads the key from the variable named in bearer_token_env_var — no interpolation syntax. Verify with `codex mcp list`.
notes.gemini: Streamable HTTP needs httpUrl; plain url means SSE. The CLI defaults to project scope, hence --scope user. Check with `/mcp` in a session.
notes.cursor: Cursor expands ${'{'}env:VAR{'}'} in headers. Restart Cursor after exporting the variable so it inherits it, then enable the server under Settings → MCP.
notes.vscode: VS Code asks for the key once and stores it encrypted. ${'{'}env:…{'}'} in headers is currently sent literally by VS Code, so this uses a prompted input instead.
notes.claudeDesktop: Claude Desktop's config file runs local servers only, so mcp-remote bridges to this endpoint (Node.js required). The key is written into the file — keep it private. Restart Claude after saving.
notes.windsurf: Newer builds read ~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json; older Windsurf builds ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json. Refresh the MCP list in Cascade after saving.
notes.opencode: oauth: false stops opencode trying OAuth against a key-authenticated server. Place it in opencode.json at the project root, or globally.
notes.zed: Zed has no environment-variable expansion in headers, so the key is written into settings.json. Or add it from Settings → AI → MCP Servers.
notes.http: Any MCP client that speaks Streamable HTTP works: POST JSON-RPC with the bearer header. This call answers who the key acts as — a quick way to test a key.
